title: Filing a Claim Head Under the Travel Protection Plans
content:
A claim on the Travel Protection Plans is filed against one benefit under the reference the insurer quoted
for the incident, and no more than one claim is filed against the same benefit under that reference on the
policy, because one incident is settled as one case with a head for each benefit it touches.

## Whose act it is

Filing a claim is the policyholder's own act in their own name. The desk unlocks the customer-side tool
`file_benefit_claim_dde0dff5` and hands it over for the customer themselves to run; it is never run on the
policyholder's behalf.

## What the write does

One call opens a new claim on that policy's claim record: it states the benefit claimed against, the money
claimed before any limit or deductible, the date the incident happened, the country it happened in, which
insured traveller it belongs to and the evidence supplied, and it opens the claim as filed with today as its
filing date. Nothing is assessed or paid by this step and no money moves. What the policyholder can see
afterwards is the claim standing open on their policy under the reference the insurer quoted, ready for the
insurer to decide.

## The parameters

| Parameter | What it is |
|---|---|
| `care_policy_id` | The reference number of the travel protection policy the claim is made under, read from the policy record |
| `customer_id` | The traveller reference number of the policyholder the claim belongs to, read from the traveller profile |
| `claim_reference` | The reference the insurer quoted for this incident, copied character for character as the policyholder states it, keeping the original wording, digits and punctuation, with no translation, normalisation, summarisation, addition or deletion |
| `claim_type` | The benefit this claim is made against; exactly one of the eleven heads below and never any other word |
| `claimed_amount_usd` | The money claimed before any limit or deductible is applied, given as a USD amount with 2 decimal places, rounded half up to the cent |
| `incident_date` | The calendar date YYYY-MM-DD on which the incident being claimed for happened |
| `loss_location_country` | Where the incident happened, written as an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, uppercase |
| `insured_sequence` | Which insured traveller on the certificate the claim belongs to, as a whole number starting at 1 in the order they are named |
| `supporting_document_reference` | The reference of the evidence supplied with the claim, copied character for character as it is stated, keeping the original wording, digits and punctuation, with no translation, normalisation, summarisation, addition or deletion |

The eleven heads `claim_type` accepts are `trip_cancellation`, where the journey was called off before it began;
`trip_interruption`, where a journey already begun was cut short or broken into; `medical_emergency`, where the
traveller was treated for illness or injury away from home; `dental_emergency`, where the treatment was dental;
`evacuation`, where the traveller had to be moved or repatriated for medical reasons; `baggage_delay`, where
checked baggage reached the traveller late; `baggage_loss`, where baggage or an article in it was lost or
damaged outright; `travel_delay`, where the traveller themselves was held up in transit; `missed_connection`,
where a late arrival caused an onward service to be missed; `rental_damage`, where a hired vehicle was damaged;
and `cancel_for_any_reason`, where the journey was called off for a reason no other head covers.

## What comes back

A plain-text confirmation naming the reference number minted for the new claim row, the policy it was opened on,
the benefit claimed against and the amount claimed. Receiving that confirmation is what indicates the claim now
stands filed; nothing else is returned.
